title: Remembering the square
bodyMd:
A fictional neighbourhood collected oral histories of a square before its redevelopment. Older residents remembered it as lively and welcoming, while some younger residents recalled avoiding it because traffic made crossing difficult. An interviewer initially tried to decide which account was the true one. A colleague suggested that the accounts might concern different periods, times of day and experiences of mobility.

The project began asking narrators to locate memories more precisely. This did not remove disagreements, but it made some understandable. A busy meeting place for one person could also be a barrier for another. The resulting exhibition placed contrasting accounts beside photographs and street plans. Its aim was not to average the memories into a single neutral story, but to show how one public space could support unequal experiences and changing meanings.
